display.purpose: The wordmark only — Archivo Black. Never reused for section headings or labels.

headline.purpose: Section headings that need editorial weight — Playfair Display. 'How it Works' h2 and similar.

title.purpose: Large data numbers in stat cards and podium XP — Playfair Display 700. Cast-in-metal feel.

body.purpose: All readable copy, metadata, table cells, nav, taglines — Inter 15px.

label.purpose: Axis labels, rank positions, step numbers, column headers — IBM Plex Mono uppercase +0.1em tracking.

shadows.name: whisper
shadows.purpose: Pill at rest. Barely-there material hint.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Light card float — archived notes, subtle surface lift.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Card hover state — step cards, squad cards. Surface rises to meet cursor.

shadows.name: strong-hover
shadows.purpose: Step card hover — slightly deeper than standard hover.

shadows.name: gold-haze
shadows.purpose: First-place podium card only. The system's one chromatic shadow.

shadows.name: fab
shadows.purpose: Settings FAB at rest. Full elevation — the one always-floating element.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Color/border transitions on hover — links, chips, segmented controls.

motion.name: state-std
motion.purpose: Standard state change — button backgrounds, card borders.

motion.name: menu-slide
motion.purpose: Mobile nav open/close. Material standard easing.

motion.name: hand-reach
motion.purpose: Hand images entering on page load. Exponential ease-out from off-screen.

motion.name: hand-float
motion.purpose: Idle float animation on hands after entry.

motion.name: word-rise
motion.purpose: Wordmark letter entrance — slight overshoot for presence.

motion.name: glint
motion.purpose: Wordmark glint sweep — periodic, subtle, 12s period.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.note: 2-col stats grid, reduced padding, mobile hand positions.

breakpoints.name: small
breakpoints.note: Further padding reduction, collapsed archived-note facts.

components.name: Primary CTA Button
components.description: Gold-filled pill button. Used for Connect Wallet and the hero CTA. Gold is the only filled color in light surfaces.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { appearance: none; background: #F0BD5E; color: #2A2004; border: 1px solid #F0BD5E; border-radius: 999px; padding: 8px 18px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: filter .16s, background .2s, color .2s, border-color .2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.05); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F9DDA0; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Neutral outline pill button. Board footer pagination, secondary actions. Never competes with the gold primary.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { appearance: none; background: #FFFFFF; color: #12161F; border: 1px solid #E7E0D2; border-radius: 999px; padding: 10px 24px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color .15s, color .15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #c0b8ac; color: #12161F; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F0BD5E; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Gold Gradient Button
components.description: Gradient gold pill button for secondary CTAs with more visual weight — copy referral link, share actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-gold-grad { appearance: none; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #F9DDA0, #F0BD5E); color: #2A2004; border: 1px solid #F0BD5E; border-radius: 999px; padding: 10px 24px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: filter .15s, background .2s, color .2s; } .ds-btn-gold-grad:hover { filter: brightness(1.04); } .ds-btn-gold-grad:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F0BD5E; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Season Chip
components.description: Pill-shaped season selector. Inactive: muted text, light border. Active: navy 1.5px border, ink text, 600 weight.
components.css: .ds-chip-wrap { display: flex; gap: 6px; } .ds-chip { appearance: none; background: transparent; color: #7C7768; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12.5px; padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; transition: color .15s, border-color .15s; } .ds-chip:hover { color: #12161F; border-color: #E7E0D2; } .ds-chip--active { color: #12161F; font-weight: 600; border: 1.5px solid #0E1729; }

components.name: Podium Card – First Place

components.name: Live Pill
components.description: Season status indicator in the hero. Fully rounded, paper background, pulsing green dot for live state.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #E7E0D2; border-radius: 999px; padding: 7px 16px 7px 12px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; color: #7C7768; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(20,16,4,.04); } .ds-pill b { color: #12161F; font-weight: 600; } .ds-pill__live { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; color: #15803D; font-weight: 600; } .ds-pill__dot { display: block; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: #22C55E; animation: ds-pulse 2.4s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%,100%{opacity:1} 50%{opacity:.35} }

narrative.overview:
StakeMyGold is a leaderboard where participation is a bet on future value — XP accumulates like gold in a vault, and this interface communicates that gravity. The visual system pairs a deep navy that reads as sealed, authoritative darkness with a warm, measured gold that signals real achievement rather than decoration. These are not 'cool crypto colors' — they are the palette of a treasury: serious, considered, earned.

The surface layer — cream, paper, near-white — keeps the day-to-day experience warm and legible. Navy is reserved for command surfaces (the header, the referral block, the mobile nav). Gold appears exactly as often as it should: to mark live status, to highlight the user's own rank, to crown the podium leader. Its restraint is its power.

Typography operates in three registers: Archivo Black for the wordmark alone (a stamp, not a label), Playfair Display for editorial weight (section headings, large stat numbers — these feel cast, not typed), and IBM Plex Mono for data precision (rank positions, step labels, stat axis labels — this is the ledger typeface). Inter handles everything else: approachable, neutral, fast to scan.
keyCharacteristics: Navy + warm gold as the only authority pairing — not gradient-washed, not glassy
Three-typeface system with strict role assignment: stamped / cast / measured / readable
Gold used as certification, not wallpaper — scarcity maintained across every surface
Flat-by-default depth with state-responsive shadows (hover, elevation, focus)
Podium ranking inherits real metal semantics: gold / silver / bronze, not arbitrary hues

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Gold (#F0BD5E) marks exactly one thing per context: the active state, the ranked leader, the live signal, the primary CTA. When two gold elements compete for attention on the same screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Warm Neutrals Rule
rules.body: No cool grays. Every neutral — from the page background to the divider line to secondary text — has a warm undertone. If a gray reads as 'digital' or 'cool', it is out of palette.

rules.name: The Three-Register Rule
rules.body: Playfair for editorial weight. IBM Plex Mono for data precision. Inter for everything readable. Archivo Black for the wordmark alone. Mixing these — using Mono for headings, or Playfair for body copy — breaks the register system.

rules.name: The Tracking Inversion Rule
rules.body: Display and title type tracks tightly (negative). Label type tracks openly (positive). Body type tracks neutrally. Tight tracking = large and present; open tracking = small and precise.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Shadows exist only as a response to interaction (hover) or a structural hierarchy decision (the FAB, the first podium card). A shadow at rest is a hierarchy claim the element must earn.

rules.name: The Gold Haze Exception
rules.body: The first-place podium card earns a warm chromatic shadow. It is the only card with a colored shadow — all other hover shadows are near-black tinted warm. The exception is the rule.

dos: Do use gold (#F0BD5E) at ≤15% visible surface coverage. It is a signal, not a theme.
Do use IBM Plex Mono in uppercase with 0.1em letter-spacing for all data labels, rank positions, and axis labels.
Do use Playfair Display for section headings and large data numbers — this is the 'weight' register, not Inter Bold.
Do keep all neutral colors warm-toned. If a gray doesn't have an ochre or amber undertone, it is out of palette.
Do use 999px radius for all interactive controls (buttons, chips, tags) and 14–18px radius for content containers. No middle ground.
Do let shadows appear only on hover, focus, or explicit structural elevation (podium first card, FAB). Surfaces are flat at rest.
Do reserve the navy (#0E1729) for command surfaces: header, referral CTA block, mobile nav. Never use it for content cards.
donts: Don't use gradient text. Emphasis comes from size, weight, or the Playfair Display register — not a gradient fill on text.
Don't add a colored border-left above 1px on general content cards. The .stat.me left accent (3px) is the single permitted exception.
Don't use Inter Bold or Inter Black for headings that should use Playfair Display. The serif register exists precisely to avoid Inter at display sizes.
Don't use cool-toned grays. #7C7768 (Warm Muted) is the floor for secondary text — anything cooler breaks the palette's thermal consistency.
Don't apply box shadows to surfaces at rest. A shadow at rest is a hierarchy claim that erodes the system's flat-by-default integrity.
Don't use Archivo Black for anything except the wordmark. It is the stamp; using it elsewhere dilutes it.
Don't introduce a fourth neutral background color. The system has three: --bg (#FDFCFA), --cream (#F8F6F2), --paper (#FFFFFF).
